vulnerabilities.description: Temporary files created with default system permissions. On multi-user systems, temp files could be world-readable before cleanup. The writeFileSync() uses default mode 0o666 (readable by all). Mitigated by immediate cleanup in finally block.
Session data stored in plaintext JSON without encryption. While currently non-sensitive data, any future sensitive information could be exposed.
Memory/configuration data stored in plaintext JSON without encryption. Acceptable for current use case but not recommended for any sensitive data.
Missing security headers configuration. No Content-Security-Policy (CSP), X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, or other security headers configured.
Weak ID generation using Math.random().toString(36). While acceptable for calculator results, uses non-cryptographic randomness.

recommendations: Add HTTP security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options) to next.config
Use crypto.getRandomValues() instead of Math.random() for ID generation in saved-results.ts
Set restrictive file permissions (0o600) on temporary files in github-safe.js
Add npm security scanning to CI/CD pipeline (snyk or npm audit)
Document security posture: static site with no backend, database, or authentication
Encrypt sensitive configuration if ever stored in session.js or memory.js

findings.hardcoded_secrets: PASS - No API keys, passwords, or tokens found
findings.sql_injection: PASS - No SQL queries or database layer
findings.api_security: PASS - No backend API calls except Google services
findings.input_validation: PASS - Input validation via masking functions
findings.data_storage: ACCEPTABLE - localStorage used for non-sensitive data only

summary: This is a static HTML/JavaScript calculator platform with no backend, database, or authentication. The architecture significantly reduces attack surface. No hardcoded secrets, SQL injection, XSS vulnerabilities, or authentication issues found. Main findings are minor: missing security headers and unencrypted local storage (appropriate for non-sensitive data). Code follows security best practices for public-facing calculator applications.
